cards.text: Paul's a prisoner, friend, and Festus, the governor, has him brought before King Agrippa and Bernice, who comes with Agrippa, in a hall packed with commanders and leading men (Acts 25:23). Festus has to send Paul on with NOTHING definite to write about him, so he wants this hearing to give him something, like a man with a report due and a blank page (Acts 25:25-26). Now King Agrippa turns to Paul.

cards.question: King Agrippa speaks first. What does he tell Paul he has permission to do?

Paul stretches out his hand and begins his defense. He tells King Agrippa he considers himself fortunate to stand before him and defend himself against all the accusations of the Jews. Why is he especially glad it's this king?

answers.text: The king knows Jewish customs well
The king owes Paul a favor
The king has already freed him once

cards.question: Paul says the Jews have known him since his earliest childhood, and they know he lived as a Pharisee, in the strictest sect of their religion. Then he gets to the charge itself. What does Paul say he's on trial because of?

answers.text: His hope in God's promise to their fathers
His teaching against the temple in Jerusalem
His refusal to honor the laws of Rome

cards.text: Paul says it's the promise the twelve tribes hope to see fulfilled as they serve God day and night, and it's because of this hope that he's accused by the Jews. Then he asks the room, "Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?"

Then Paul says, "So then, I too was convinced that I ought to do all I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth." Friend, the man on trial just started reading his OWN rap sheet out loud. On purpose.

cards.question: Paul says that when the saints in Jerusalem were condemned to death, he cast his vote against them.

cards.text: Paul says he put many of the saints in prison and had them punished in the synagogues, and in his raging fury he went to foreign cities to persecute them. That's what he was doing on his way to Damascus, with the authority and commission of the chief priests.

About noon, a light from heaven brighter than the sun shines around Paul and his companions, and they all fall to the ground. Then a voice speaks to him in Hebrew, and it calls him Saul, which is Paul's other name (Acts 13:9).

cards.question: On the Damascus road, the voice from heaven calls him by name twice: Saul, Saul. What does the voice ask him?

answers.text: Why do you run from Me

cards.text: Then the voice adds, "It is hard for you to kick against the goads." Friend, that's kicking the kitchen counter because you're mad at it, and the counter is FINE.

cards.question: On the Damascus road, Paul asks, "Who are You, Lord?" The Lord answers that He is ___, the one Paul is persecuting.
Jesus tells Saul to get up and stand on his feet. He has appeared to appoint Saul as a servant and a ___ of what he has seen.

cards.text: Jesus says He'll rescue Saul from his own people and from the Gentiles, and He's sending Saul to them to open their eyes, so they may turn from darkness to light. Saul used to travel on orders from the chief priests, and now he's on orders from Jesus Himself, friend, and that's a CAREER CHANGE.

cards.question: Jesus is sending Saul so that people may turn from the power of Satan to God and receive forgiveness of sins. What else may they receive among those sanctified by faith in Jesus?

cards.text: Paul tells the king, "So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision." From Damascus and Jerusalem to all of Judea and then the Gentiles, he declared that people should repent and turn to God.

cards.question: Paul says that as he preached, he told people their repentance didn't need to show up in what they do.

cards.text: For this reason, Paul says, the Jews seized him in the temple courts and tried to kill him. But he's had God's help to this day, and here he stands, testifying to small and great alike.

cards.question: Paul says he's saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses, Israel's leader, said would happen. What did they say about the Christ?

answers.text: He would suffer and rise first from the dead
He would conquer Rome with a mighty army
He would rule forever without ever suffering

cards.question: Paul says the Christ would proclaim light only to the people of Israel.

cards.text: At this stage of Paul's defense, Festus doesn't raise his hand. He just YELLS, "You are insane, Paul!"

cards.question: Festus shouts that something is driving Paul to madness. What does Festus blame?

cards.text: Paul answers, "I am not insane, most excellent Festus; I am speaking words of truth and sobriety." Friend, the man gets called insane in front of a KING and he still calls the guy MOST EXCELLENT.

cards.question: Paul says the events he's been describing were done in a corner, where King Agrippa could easily have missed them.

cards.text: Then Paul asks him straight out, "King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do." He asked AND answered, like a text that says "You coming tonight? You're coming."

cards.question: Paul just asked King Agrippa if he believes the prophets. How does the king answer Paul?

answers.text: He asks if Paul can persuade him to become a Christian that fast
He says he gave up on the prophets long ago
He tells the guards to take Paul away right now

cards.text: Paul says, "Short time or long," and then he tells the king what he wishes to God for everyone in that room.

cards.question: Paul tells King Agrippa what he wishes to God for him and all who hear him that day. What is it?

answers.text: That they would all become what he is
That they would all set him free today
That they would all judge him fairly

cards.text: Then Paul adds one exception: "except for these chains." Friend, he wants them to have everything he's got, except the jewelry.
Then the king and the governor rise, along with Bernice and everyone seated with them. When a king stands up, friend, the meeting is OVER.

cards.question: On their way out, the king and the others say to one another that Paul has done nothing worthy of death or imprisonment.
King Agrippa tells Festus that Paul could have been ___ if he had not appealed to Caesar.
